newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Q3 current account deficit widens.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Q3 current account deficit widens.

text.p: The current account deficit in Israel's balance of payments widened in the third quarter to $1.746 billion, the Central Bureau of Statistics said on Thursday.
In January-September, the current account deficit was $4.712 billion against $3.525 billion in the year-earlier period.
Direct foreign investment in the nine months totalled $1.623 billion against $1.338 billion in the same period last year.
Net foreign debt was $21.314 billion at the end of September, against $20.191 billion at the end of 1995.

The statistics bureau also said Israeli exports to the Palestinian self-ruled areas totalled $1.141 billion in the nine months against $1.130 billion in the same period last year. Imports totalled $140 million against $276 million a year earlier.
Israel receives the bulk of its American aid in the fourth quarter, which will significantly reduce the current account deficit in the final three months of the year.
